title: Automated UI Regression Testing for Legacy Web Portals
business: Enterprise software teams maintaining complex legacy web applications that lack structured metadata for automated testing.
problem: Manual QA teams struggle to identify visual regressions in legacy portals where DOM structures are dynamic, obfuscated, or inconsistent, leading to high maintenance costs for brittle test scripts.
solution: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 provides an image-text-to-text capability that interprets visual UI states alongside historical context. By feeding screenshots of the legacy portal into the model, the system identifies functional discrepancies between expected and actual UI states without relying on fragile CSS selectors.
steps: Capture baseline screenshots of stable application states to serve as visual ground truth.
Integrate the model into the CI/CD pipeline to process current build screenshots against baseline images.
Enable thinking preservation to allow the model to reference previous test iterations for consistent state tracking.
Generate natural language reports detailing identified visual deviations or functional UI errors.
outcome: Reduced reliance on brittle element selectors and faster identification of visual regressions in legacy environments.
limitation: The model's reliance on visual interpretation may lead to false positives if UI elements are intentionally dynamic or animated; verify results by cross-referencing visual output with backend logs.
